Fail! Democrats established the enhanced Affordable Care Act (ACA) healthcare subsidies during the COVID-19 pandemic and explicitly set them to expire at the end of 2025.

These subsidies, known as enhanced premium tax credits, were first created in the 2021 American Rescue Plan Act—a $1.9 trillion COVID relief package passed by a Democrat-controlled Congress and signed by President Joe Biden—to make ACA marketplace plans more affordable. The law expanded eligibility to households earning above 400% of the federal poverty level (about $62,600 for an individual or $124,800 for a family of four in 2025) and capped premium contributions at 8.5% of income, with some low-income enrollees paying $0. This boosted enrollment from 11.4 million in 2020 to 24.3 million in 2025, with 92% of enrollees receiving subsidies.

In 2022, Democrats extended these benefits through December 31, 2025, via the Inflation Reduction Act, another partisan bill passed without Republican votes. Both laws were temporary COVID-era measures, with no automatic renewal built in. If they expire as scheduled, the Congressional Budget Office estimates 4 million people could lose coverage by 2034, and KFF analysis shows average premiums doubling (from $888 to $1,904 annually), with some states facing 75%+ increases—hitting red states like Texas and Florida hardest.
